description: Tracks ongoing social interactions, NPC relationships, and conversation state. NPCs should persist here even when not currently present — this is the relationship ledger, not just the active scene.

fields.scene: string or null — description of the current social situation (1-2 sentences), or null if no active social interaction
fields.npcs_present: array of objects — NPCs currently in the scene: { name, role (e.g. 'merchant', 'guard captain', 'innkeeper'), attitude (hostile|unfriendly|neutral|friendly|helpful), notes (string — relevant history, current mood, what they know) }
fields.npcs_known: array of objects — NPCs not currently present but known to the player from prior interactions: same structure as npcs_present; preserves relationship state across scenes
fields.conversation_state: string or null — what stage the current conversation is at (e.g. 'negotiating price', 'awaiting response to offer', 'player presented evidence', 'guard suspicious')
fields.stakes: string or null — what is at stake in the current interaction (e.g. 'safe passage through the gate', 'hiring the guide', 'learning the baron's secret')
fields.persuasion_progress: string or null — summary of persuasion or diplomacy progress so far in this interaction

notes: npcs_known persists important NPCs across scenes — a merchant the player met three sessions ago should still be here.
Clear the scene and conversation_state fields when the social interaction ends, but keep npcs_known updated.
If the player changes location and the NPCs did not follow, clear npcs_present and the scene — but preserve them in npcs_known.
Attitude changes from the outcome should be reflected immediately in both npcs_present and npcs_known.
